title: Digital Banking Tools for Better Business Cash Flow | Landmark
summary: Without a clear & current view of their finances, owners may rely on spreadsheets, disconnected systems or outdated balances.
body_markdown:
For small business owners, cash flow is more than money coming in and going out. It affects the ability to pay employees, purchase inventory, cover operating expenses and confidently plan for what comes next. Even a profitable business can experience challenges when the timing of its incoming revenue does not align with upcoming payments.


The right digital banking tools can make that balancing act easier. By helping owners monitor activity, accelerate receivables, manage payments and reduce fraud risk, these solutions provide greater visibility and control over a company’s finances.


## **Why Cash-Flow Visibility Matters**


Business owners make financial decisions every day. Can the company afford to place a larger inventory order? Is there enough available cash to cover payroll? Which customer payments are still outstanding? Are any unexpected transactions affecting the account?


Without a clear and current view of their finances, owners may rely on spreadsheets, disconnected systems or outdated balances. That can make it more difficult to recognize potential shortfalls and respond before they disrupt operations.

## **Monitor Account Activity From Anywhere**


Digital access allows business owners to review balances and recent transactions without waiting for a paper statement or visiting a bank location. This visibility can be especially valuable for owners who manage multiple accounts, locations or employees.

ers can regularly monitor account activity, confirm that deposits have been received and review upcoming payments. Establishing a routine for checking accounts can help them identify cash-flow concerns earlier and reduce the chance that an unexpected transaction goes unnoticed.


Alerts can add another layer of awareness. Depending on the tools available, a business may be able to receive notifications for low balances, large transactions, incoming deposits or other important account activity. These updates help owners stay informed without constantly signing in to check their accounts.


## **Accelerate the Collection of Receivables**


The faster a business can collect and deposit customer payments, the sooner those funds may become available for operating expenses. Digital payment and deposit tools can reduce the delays associated with manually processing checks or waiting for customers to make in-person payments.


For businesses that regularly receive checks, remote deposit capabilities may allow an authorized employee to scan and submit eligible checks from the office. Electronic payment options, including ACH transactions, can also provide a more efficient way to receive recurring or business-to-business payments.


Owners should review their current collection process and ask a few important questions:


- How long does it typically take to receive customer payments?


- How quickly are those payments deposited?


- Are invoices and payment due dates communicated clearly?


- Are there opportunities to replace manual steps with electronic processes?


- Who is responsible for following up on overdue accounts?


Improving even one part of the receivables process can help shorten the amount of time between completing work and having usable funds in the account.


## **Manage Payments More Strategically**


Cash-flow management is not only about collecting money quickly. It is also about knowing when payments will leave the account and ensuring they are authorized, accurate and properly timed.


Digital tools can help businesses organize recurring expenses, schedule payments and maintain records of completed transactions. ACH services may be useful for vendor payments or direct deposit, while wire transfers can support certain time-sensitive or higher-value transactions.

Creating separate user access and approval responsibilities can help owners maintain oversight without requiring them to personally complete every task.


Businesses should regularly review who has access to their accounts, what each user is permitted to do and whether former employees have been removed. Internal processes should be updated as the company grows or responsibilities change.


## **Strengthen Protection Against Fraud**


Digital convenience should be paired with thoughtful safeguards. Business accounts can be targeted through altered checks, unauthorized electronic payments, compromised login credentials and deceptive messages designed to convince employees to send money.


Treasury management services may include tools that help businesses review or identify suspicious activity. For example, certain fraud-prevention services can compare presented payments with information previously authorized by the business. Approval controls may also require more than one person to review specific transactions before funds are released.


Technology is only one part of fraud prevention. Businesses should also establish consistent internal practices, including:


- Using strong, unique passwords and multifactor authentication


- Limiting account access to employees who need it


- Verifying unusual payment requests through a trusted contact method


- Reviewing account activity frequently


- Separating payment initiation and approval responsibilities when possible


- Training employees to recognize phishing and impersonation attempts


If something appears unusual, the business should contact its bank promptly. Fast action can be critical when addressing suspected fraud.

As a business becomes more complex, its financial needs often extend beyond basic account access. Landmark National Bank’s Treasury Express can serve as a centralized resource for eligible business clients seeking greater control over daily cash-management tasks.


Depending on the services selected, treasury management solutions can help businesses monitor accounts, initiate payments, manage receivables and strengthen internal controls. The best combination of tools will depend on factors such as transaction volume, payment methods, staffing structure and fraud exposure. A retail business that processes frequent customer payments may have different needs than a professional services firm, agricultural operation or growing company with employees in several locations.


## **Pair Digital Convenience With Personal Guidance**


Technology can simplify everyday financial tasks, but business owners should not have to determine the right solution on their own. A trusted banking partner can review how money currently moves through the company, identify inefficient processes and recommend services that align with the business’s needs.
